text:
jordan: Seeing hovercards show projects from the previous org when fast-switching in the console. Repro: open quick switcher -> switch org -> immediately hover a project card -> hover shows wrong org name/project list. Happens ~30% on my machine. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/test-hover-leak.png :eyes:
anya: repro'd this. Happens only if you hover right after switch. Client fetch seems to get stale panel HTML that includes previous org -> feels like CDN edge is serving a cached blob that doesn't vary by org. :confused:
sam: I dug into logs. X-Org-Id is hitting the backend, but the hovercard content is being served from our edge cache. Edge cache key currently includes route+id but NOT org id. If CDN strips the org header we lose tenant isolation. Adding org to cache key would fix correctness but could increase cache churn. @kai any history on why we didn't include org in vary?
kai: we intentionally avoided adding org to edge vary because hovercards are high QPS and many orgs have sparse traffic; cache cardinality explodes. The router sets an affinity tag in a header but CloudFront strips some custom headers by default. Short-term: we can invalidate/bust edge cache on org switch for hovercards. Long-term: either include org in cache key for server-rendered hovercards or move tenant-specific shading to client-side fetch.
denise: short-term cache-bust seems safest. Minimal client-side guard: when user switches org, bump a client-side org switch timestamp and append as query param to hovercard fetch so edge treats it as a distinct object. Low risk and quick to ship.
anya: can you paste the minimal patch? I can review and help ship to staging.
denise: sure, gist of the change below:
```
--- a/webapp/src/hovercard/fetch.ts
+++ b/webapp/src/hovercard/fetch.ts
@@ -1,6 +1,8 @@
-const url = `/api/hovercard?id=${id}`
+const orgTs = window.__ORG_SWITCH_TS || ''
+const url = `/api/hovercard?id=${id}${orgTs ? `&org_ts=${orgTs}` : ''}`
```
This ensures a fresh fetch after a switch without touching CDN config. Backend should treat org_ts as a no-op cache breaker.
sam: backend follow-up: add a tiny guard so if org_ts is present we bypass cached surrogate variants (or at least force a stale-while-revalidate path). I'll open PR to handle edge headers and file a ticket to add Vary: X-Org-Id on hovercard endpoint (long-term ops approval needed).
sam: also putting a small telemetry event on org-switch-triggered-hoverfetch so we can measure frequency and impact.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for canary -> staging at 2026-03-21T14:22Z :rocket:
jordan: thanks folks. Can we also add a metric hovercard_cache_miss_on_org_switch so product can see user impact? @denise @sam pls add to the PRs.
denise: will add the telemetry increment (low overhead). Taking the client patch, testing locally, then sending PR with test and changelog.
